strengths: Mercury-free high-power source addresses a documented regulatory direction (Minamata Convention pressure on mercury lamps).
Inventor-supplied laboratory results indicate competitive dose performance at reduced footprint (inventor claim — independently unverified).
Technology Overview language already validated by prior reviewer feedback as plain-language accessible.
Broad application surface: municipal, industrial process, and commercial building water all theoretically addressable from one source technology.
weaknesses: No shipping product or field installation; all performance figures are inventor-supplied and independently unverified.
Lamp lifetime under duty cycling not yet measured by a third party.
No named reactor-integration partner contacted, qualified, or engaged.
Upstream excimer-source supply chain at commercial power levels uncharacterized (Appendix C S6).
opportunities: Industrial process water as beachhead: fastest validation path, least regulatory drag.
Reactor-integration licensing into incumbent lines avoids building a reactor company first.
Third-party validation study via utility research consortium creates citable differentiation.
European exposure ahead of ACHEMA 2027 / IFAT 2028 cycle.
threats: Incumbent lamp-lifecycle economics delay switching until replacement cycles open.
Excelitas consolidation of excimer expertise (Noblelight) may raise component-supply barriers.
Unresolved upstream supply figures (recorded in Appendix C S6) leave sourcing-cost uncertainty.
